messages:
Liam (sales): NovaHealth asked for final network recommendation before we put numbers in the SOW. Key constraints: must show SNI to their TLS inspector in the DMZ, want original client IP in app logs, and prefer the path with lowest ops friction for a 5TB/month POC. Thoughts?

Nora (solutions): TL;DR: If SNI must hit their DMZ inspector, TLS must terminate before PrivateLink endpoint. That implies either: 1) terminate at their proxy then re-TLS to us (works with PrivateLink but client-ip will be the proxy/endpoint unless they re-insert X-Forwarded-For), or 2) use VPC peering/route-based path so client IPs are preserved and SNI is visible to their inline inspector.

Jin (netinfra): Quick pros/cons:
- VPC peering: preserves srcIP, simple firewalls (CIDR allow), no interface endpoint charges, but cross-account peering needs org approval and route tables updated. Good for low-latency logs and for customers who need the real source IP.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoint): great isolation and least privilege (only endpoint ENIs allowed), faster security sign-off for orgs that forbid peering, but source becomes endpoint ENI IPs -> need XFF and proxy instrumentation. Also PrivateLink has per-GB data processing charges.

Jin (netinfra): Diagram:
OnPrem -> TGW -> Spoke -> (A) Peering -> Redwood-VPC -> App
OnPrem -> TGW -> Spoke -> (B) InterfaceEndpoint -> ENI -> RedwoodPrivate

Heather (security): For their questionnaire: we should provide a concise answer for SNI/TLS handling, logging, and key custody. Suggested snippet: "Redwood Private supports TLS with customer-terminated proxies, mutual TLS to customer CAs, and integration with customer-managed KMS/HSM for key storage. We do not store plaintext customer keys and audit key operations. If TLS is inspected in-customer DMZ, customers must terminate and re-establish TLS to Redwood."

Liam (sales): They asked whether we can keep both behaviors during the POC (preserve client IP and allow their TLS inspector to see SNI) without major changes. Can we do a hybrid?

Nora (solutions): Hybrid is possible but adds complexity: e.g., put a small proxy in their VPC that terminates TLS (so inspector sees SNI), then re-TLS to Redwood over peering while preserving an X-Forwarded-For header from the proxy to surface client IPs (peering will preserve network srcIP, but if you terminate and re-TLS at the proxy, backend sees proxy srcIP unless proxy forwards XFF). Alternatively, use peering and let their inline inspector observe SNI if TLS is terminated upstream of peering. All options require a short config checklist.

Jin (netinfra): Cost delta (very rough) to drop in SOW: PrivateLink infra fees = endpoint hourly (~$0.01/hr) + data processing (~$0.01/GB). For 5TB (5,120 GB) that’s ~ $51 data processing + ~$7 endpoint = ~$60/mo, excluding cloud provider egress. Peering: no endpoint/data processing fees but cross-VPC transfer costs vary by region (estimate $0.005-$0.02/GB) -> ~$25-$100/mo. Operational overhead for peering can add ~1-2 engineer-hours initial config.

Heather (security): Also add note to SOW: if customer requires TLS inspection in their DMZ and insists on seeing client IPs, there is an expected integration task to deploy/verify proxy behavior and headers. Flag as an out-of-scope item unless included in managed onboarding.

Liam (sales): Perfect. Please give me one-paragraph text for the SOW that explains the tradeoffs and sets a default recommendation.

Nora (solutions): SOW blurb (drop-in): "Recommendation: For NovaHealths POC we recommend VPC peering to Redwood Private when preservation of original client IP in application logs and visibility of SNI to an inline TLS inspector are required. VPC peering preserves source IPs and allows the customers DMZ/TLS inspection to observe SNI without terminating/injecting TLS proxies. If the customer prefers stronger network isolation or forbids route exchange, PrivateLink is an alternative but requires TLS termination at the customer proxy (or X-Forwarded-For header insertion) and carries modest per-GB interface processing fees. The engineering handoff will include firewall allowlists, expected CIDRs, and an operations checklist."

Liam (sales): Great. Jin, can you paste the exact firewall allowlist lines we should give NetOps (customer)?

Jin (netinfra): Paste-ready snippet:
```
# If using PrivateLink (interface endpoint)
Allow outbound TCP/443 -> <interface-endpoint-subnet-cidr(s)>
Allow outbound TCP/443 -> <redwood-management-ips>  # control plane, if applicable

# If using VPC peering
Allow outbound TCP/443 -> <redwood-peering-cidr>  # peered VPC range

# Common
Deny TLS <1.2; enforce TLS 1.2+ and strong ciphers
Monitor and log X-Forwarded-For headers if using proxy termination
```

infra-bot: Ticket created RW-3971: "NovaHealth POC - network preservecip vs inspect SOW"

Liam (sales): I'll send this to NovaHealth later today. Thanks team — will loop back once they pick peering vs PrivateLink. :white_check_mark:
